data.title: Video
data.tagline: Media with moving images and a duration that plays on a page
data.description: Video can demonstrate a product action or teach a course, such as “Create a project in two minutes.” The poster should state the topic and length, and the player needs captions, sound controls, and a clear failure state.

distinctions.label: Image
distinctions.explanation: Video has time-based content, playback controls, and often sound. Image shows a single static frame.

avoid: No poster, duration, or load-failure message

lessonPractice.title: A help page uses a two-minute video to demonstrate project creation, and the steps are necessary to complete the task. What is a complete delivery?

options.label: Provide a poster, duration, controls, captions, written steps, and a load-failure state
options.feedback: Video shows motion, while captions and written steps preserve the task for muted playback, failure, and quick reference.

options.label: Autoplay with sound on page open and place pause and captions inside settings
options.feedback: Automatic sound interrupts users and consumes resources, while still failing to provide captions or alternatives.

options.label: Keep only the player and remove every required step from the surrounding page
options.feedback: Users who cannot play or hear it, or who need one step quickly, lose the information required to complete the task.

data.agentPrompt: Embed the project-creation tutorial with a poster, duration, playback, and volume controls, without sound autoplay. Add accurate captions and equivalent written steps, and verify users can complete the task if the video fails.
